title: Localizations of the integers are fields or discrete valuation rings
statement: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] Dedekind domain (that is, a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one) with fraction field $\mathbf Q$. Its prime ideals are $(0)$ and the ideals $(p)$ generated by rational primes $p$. The localization $\mathbf Z_{(0)}$ is the field $\mathbf Q$, and for every nonzero prime ideal $(p)$ the localization $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local discrete valuation ring (that is, a Noetherian local domain of Krull dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; see [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]) with maximal ideal $(p)\mathbf Z_{(p)}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), implication (1) => (2), together with Definition Tag 034W and Lemma Tag 0AUQ (a PID is Dedekind); the description of prime ideals of $\mathbf Z$ and $\mathbf Z_{(0)}=\mathbf Q$ is the elementary PID calculation used in the same lemma. The characterization of a Noetherian one-dimensional local domain as a DVR is Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr).

proof.text: Use Mathlib instance IsPrincipalIdealRing.isDedekindDomain for the Euclidean domain Z and Rat.isFractionRing for its fraction field Q. Use IsPrincipalIdealRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one with Int.not_isField for dimension one.

Apply Mathlib Ideal.isPrime_int_iff to classify the integer prime ideals. At the zero prime, Ideal.primeCompl_bot identifies the denominator monoid with the nonzero divisors. Rat.isFractionRing and Localization.algEquiv then give the Z-algebra isomorphism with Q.

For a nonzero prime P, obtain p and P=(p) from Ideal.isPrime_int_iff. IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing supplies Noetherianity and Localization.AtPrime.isLocalRing supplies locality. Apply Mathlib IsLocalization.AtPrime.isDiscreteValuationRing_of_dedekind_domain to Z and P. Finally IsLocalization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal and Ideal.map_span identify the maximal ideal with the span of the image of p.

The second classifies primes and deduces dimension one and the Dedekind conclusion. The third cites lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso for prime correspondence, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime for the local maximal ideal, and the existing localization-normal-domain and localization-noetherian leaves. The fourth cites the existing one-dimensional normal-local DVR criterion lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr (Stacks 00PD) and records it as a generic tool use. No new nodes were added.

lean.statement: theorem prime_localizations_dvr : IsDedekindDomain ℤ ∧ ringKrullDim ℤ = 1 ∧ IsFractionRing ℤ ℚ ∧ (∀ P : Ideal ℤ, P.IsPrime ↔ P = ⊥ ∨ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ P = Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}) ∧ Nonempty (Localization.AtPrime (⊥ : Ideal ℤ) ≃ₐ[ℤ] ℚ) ∧ (∀ (P : Ideal ℤ) [P.IsPrime], P ≠ ⊥ → IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime P) ∧ IsLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime P) ∧ IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime P) ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ P = Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)} ∧ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime P) = Ideal.span {algebraMap ℤ (Localization.AtPrime P) (p : ℤ)})
